coordinate_space: Each edit uses integer coordinates in its own input image stage after EXIF orientation. A pixel or colour edit addresses the content stage, the source after EXIF orientation, because the host places both before the quarter-turns, reflections and crop that carry them; a colour edit addresses every pixel of that stage and changes no dimension. A number parameter carries a finite JSON number within its declared range, such as an angle in degrees or a rectangle normalized to its stage; a JSON integer is accepted and passed through unchanged.

folder.values: "original" (each photograph's own original's folder) or {path}, an absolute path to an existing folder

metadata.notes: none: no EXIF; copyright: Artist and Copyright; no_location: every supported field but the GPS group; all: every supported field; every level but none also writes Orientation 1, ColorSpace sRGB, the output's pixel dimensions, ExifVersion and Software

optimise.notes: jpeg: progressive scans, optimised Huffman tables and trellis quantisation with the standard tables; webp: the slowest, best method; tiff: lossless Deflate with the horizontal predictor

sharpen.notes: output sharpening, null for none: {medium, amount}, applied after resizing at the output's size to luminance only, on the encoded codes, adding no colour fringes; screen sharpens with a small fixed radius, matte and glossy with one from pixels_per_inch (300 ppi when it is null), matte the stronger; low, standard and high scale the amount

size.values: {fit: full}, {fit: long_edge, pixels} or {fit: within, width, height}

suffix.notes: no path separator, no control character and no leading dot

export_settings.notes: ExportSettings, one flat JSON object. Every field that applies to the chosen format is required, a nullable one as null when it is unset; every field that does not apply is left out, and sending one, even as null, is validation naming it; so jpeg has quality, chroma and limit_bytes and no bit_depth, webp has quality and limit_bytes, and tiff has bit_depth and none of quality, chroma or limit_bytes. Every refusal is validation naming the field as settings.<field> in the message and in data.field. The output size scales the output stage, after orientation, transforms and crop, by one factor never above 1 and rounds each side to whole pixels, half up, at least 1, so an output is never enlarged. A file is named <original stem><suffix>.<extension> (jpg, webp or tif), counting up <stem><suffix>-2.<extension> and so on while a name is taken, reading at most 64 names; nothing is ever replaced.

markers.notes: authority: "permissions" marks a method only a client with permission authority may call at all; any other client is refused forbidden before its handler runs or a retry is answered (a method that needs it for one argument value, such as usage.set's opt-in, is not marked and says so in its notes). read_only is on every method: true only when it changes nothing at all, no catalog, library, session, preference, flag, job or file state (holding a wait is a read, and so is a call whose only effect is a derived, disposable record: a preview, an analysis report or the folder index listed again; mutates says only that a method carries a mutation envelope, and many methods change something without one, such as view.set, draft.* or job.cancel). reversible marks every method whose read_only is false and no read: true when its change can be put back through this API (history.undo, library.undo, the same method with the earlier value, removing exactly what it created, or setting the caller's own session state again; every edit.* and mask.* action is a history entry, and a task.* only adds a job and outputs nothing references, which job.cancel stops and releases), false when it discards something no call brings back or acts where Luxforge cannot take it back (a deletion, a secret, collected artifacts, released candidates, another client's session, a file written outside the catalog, a permission change, an installed update). network: true marks a method that can reach the network, never a read, omitted otherwise. images lists the dotted fields of a method's answer that hold the path of a JPEG the owner wrote for display; job_images, on job.read and job.wait, is {kind, fields}: kind is the answer's field naming the job's kind and fields maps a job kind to the dotted fields of the answer that hold such a path once its result is ready. A field absent from an answer holds none. An export's output is never marked.

batch.apply-settings.notes: starts a batch-settings job, answering {job_id, status, deduplicated}, whose result is {done, skipped: [{asset_id, code, reason}], settings_skipped?: [{asset_id, settings: [{action, parameter?, reason}]}]}: the set is either inline settings with their origin ({kind: preset, name, preset_id?} or {kind: paste, source, source_asset?}) or a library preset_id, read once, whose origin is {kind: preset, name, preset_id}; exactly one of settings and preset_id, and origin only with settings; it is checked once as edit.apply-settings checks it, so an unknown, non-presettable or overlapping action or a refused field refuses the submission, and a step whose module does not apply to a photograph's kind is skipped for that photograph; then it is applied to each photograph targets names, one at a time, exactly as edit.apply-settings applies it (against the photograph's current revision, by the envelope's actor under the request identity <request_id>/<asset_id>), analysis steps such as Auto tone running after the field patches and recomputed per photograph; so each done photograph has its own entry labelled by the origin (Preset: <name> or Paste settings from <source>) and records an event naming it and its revision; settings_skipped lists the settings left out of a done photograph because they do not apply to it; skipped names every photograph left out: removed (in Removed), draft-open (the caller holds a draft on it), history-selected (the caller previews its history), locked (a running task such as task.fill-generative holds it locked), not-applicable (none of the set's settings apply to it), unchanged (it already has them) or the code and message edit.apply-settings refuses it with; a stack that needs its source prepared is prepared first, one photograph at a time; targets are photographs by id, by their originals' paths or index rows, or the photographs selected in the caller's view; an unknown preset or photograph is validation; the job's detail is the entry label and the photograph count; while it runs job.read's result is the report so far and its progress reads n of N; job.cancel stops it between photographs or during deferred analysis, keeping every one done; a retry after a restart applies nothing twice; resource-limit past 50,000 photographs or when 4 library jobs already wait; the job records one event as it ends, however it ends, naming its job_id

batch.export.notes: starts a batch-export job, answering {job_id, status, deduplicated}, whose result is {done, written: [{asset_id, path, renderer, quality?}], skipped: [{asset_id, code, reason}]}: each photograph targets names, one at a time, has its current entry exported exactly as export.write exports it with settings, the same for every photograph (refused at once, before any job, for a chosen folder that is not an existing directory, validation with data.notice folder-missing), through the GPU tile service or the reference renderer, into settings.folder: each photograph's own original's folder for original, or the chosen folder; each file is named by the export's rule from its original's name, <stem><suffix>.<extension>, else <stem><suffix>-2.<extension> and so on per folder, at most 64 names read, and never replacing a file; each written file names the renderer that rendered it as export.write's result does ({record: gpu, reason: null}, or {record: reference, reason} with why the GPU did not, no reason on an owner with no GPU provider) and its quality as export.write's result names it, and records an event under the request; skipped names every photograph left out: removed (in Removed), or the code and message export.write refuses it with, such as source-unavailable for a missing or offline original, a refusing notice's code with its words (folder-missing for a derived photograph with original, webp-too-large or tiff-too-large for an output the format cannot hold), limit-unreachable when no quality fits the size limit, and conflict when every name is taken; a source that is not prepared is prepared first through the one preparation path, one photograph at a time, replacing the editor's prepared source; targets as batch.apply-settings'; while it runs job.read's result is the report so far and its progress reads n of N; job.cancel stops it between photographs, or within the one being exported, whose temporary file is removed, keeping every file written; resource-limit past 50,000 photographs or when 4 library jobs already wait; the job records one event as it ends, however it ends, naming its job_id

edit.apply-settings.notes: applies a settings set as one history entry labelled by its origin: `Preset: <name>`, or `Paste settings from <source>` with a source over 64 characters shortened in the middle. Each key of settings names a field-patch action and its fields, or a declared analysis action and an empty object. The host runs patches in key order, then analysis steps such as Auto tone separately for this photo, against the intermediate stack, as it would run that action alone, and commits the result once. Fields the set does not name keep their values, masked layers are unchanged, and a set that changes nothing is a reported no-op. A step whose module does not apply to the photo's kind, and a field another control supersedes on the photo's global target, are skipped and listed under skipped in the result. Auto without usable tonal range is also skipped. An unknown, non-presettable or unavailable action, an overlapping analysis/field set or another refused field refuses the whole set and writes nothing, and so does an action whose module is offered only under an experiment flag that is off, as not-ready with data.flag naming the flag.

optional.amount: Preset strength: omitted or 100 preserves the set; numbers scale from their module defaults and clamp to bounds, identity curves blend y from x. Unsupported fields and analysis steps require 100. Unnamed fields keep their values.

optional.blacks: moves the black point, crushing or lifting the darkest tones, separately from Shadows
optional.contrast: changes midtone separation with a fixed pivot at encoded mid-grey using a smooth, monotone S-curve
optional.exposure: on a JPEG shifts each linear-light channel by the value in stops on the scene scale measured from Lightroom Classic's Exposure: the deepest shadows and values past white take the plain gain, the midtones about 1.4 times the stops, and the highlights roll off towards white rather than clipping; the input is the rendered image decoded through the sRGB transfer function, so this corrects a rendered image and cannot recover detail a clipped plateau no longer holds. On a RAW photo it multiplies the developed scene-linear planes by 2^EV, which stay unclipped until the terminal boundary, before the tone curve and the Look render them. It is the one exposure on every kind: the RAW development carries none
optional.highlights: smoothly lifts or crushes the image's bright tones while leaving pure white exactly unchanged
optional.mask: the mask this edit applies through; omit it to edit the layer that applies everywhere. The global layer and each mask are distinct targets, so this action commits or updates one layer per target
optional.saturation: scales chroma uniformly about the achromatic axis; -100 is neutral grayscale, not merely a strong desaturation
optional.shadows: smoothly lifts or crushes the image's dark tones while leaving pure black exactly unchanged
optional.temperature: a relative warm/cool correction of the photo as rendered (a JPEG as decoded; on a RAW photo only through a mask, over the development, since a RAW photo's global white balance is the source development's), not a camera Kelvin value: 0 is the image's existing rendering and nothing here recovers or reproduces the camera's own white balance. Positive temperature warms the image, raising red and lowering blue; negative cools it. Each channel shifts by its own frozen stops on the scene scale Exposure uses, measured from Lightroom Classic, so white stays white and the cast lives in the midtones and shadows
optional.tint: a relative green/magenta correction of the photo as rendered (a JPEG as decoded; on a RAW photo only through a mask, over the development, since a RAW photo's global white balance is the source development's), not a camera Kelvin or tint value: 0 is the image's existing rendering. Positive tint is magenta, raising red and blue and lowering green; negative is green. Each channel shifts by its own frozen stops on the scene scale, measured from Lightroom Classic, adding to Temperature's
optional.vibrance: raises chroma more for near-neutral colour than for colour already close to the sRGB gamut edge, with reduced gain in a skin-like hue band; that hue weighting is a colour heuristic, not skin detection, and is not a promise about every skin tone
optional.whites: moves the white point, extending or protecting highlight clipping, separately from Highlights

edit.set-grain.notes: merges the named Grain fields into the stack's one Grain layer. A missing key means that field's own default (amount 0, size 25, roughness 50). The host places the layer at the end of the stack, after the geometry tail and the vignette, on the first commit whose merged amount is non-zero, and updates it there in place afterwards; a patch that changes nothing is a reported no-op, and a first set whose merged amount is still 0 commits no layer at all. Offered only while the experiment flag grain is on: while it is off this action is refused as not-ready with data.flag naming the flag, called directly, as a draft's action or as a step of a settings set; the stack's stored layers render the same either way.

optional.amount: the grain's strength: luminance grain weighted by tone, vanishing at black and at each pixel's white, mean-preserving and colour-preserving. 0 is the exact identity whatever size and roughness hold, and a missing key defaults to 0.
optional.roughness: the grain's regularity at fixed strength: fine and even at 0, uneven and clumped at 100; a missing key defaults to 50.
optional.size: the grain's particle size, in pixels of the full-resolution output stage: about one pixel at 0, six at 100, unchanged by a crop; a missing key defaults to 25.

each photograph is filed by its own camera-local capture day as its header records it when it is developed, so a file the index does not list gets its day too: {kind: place, name} files it in the top-level folder named after its year ("2026"), then name, then its day ("12 Sep"), and one with no capture time in the top-level "Undated", then name; {kind: existing, folder_id} files it in that folder, and with days: true in its day's folder inside it (the folder itself with no capture time); {kind: new, name, parent_id?} makes one folder; each developed pick names folder_id, the folder its photograph is in (a linked or relinked photograph's own), and chosen_folder_id, the folder its choice named: the place or existing folder over the day folder it was filed in, else folder_id; each folder of a path is found by its name among its siblings ignoring case, or made by the batch that first puts a photograph in it, in that batch's change, and a place never adds a number to its name; a place folder or new folder Develop makes records the span of the events it is made from, and their key when made from one, a year or day folder records none, and a found folder is not changed; an existing folder must exist, a place's and a new folder's name are checked as folder.create's and a new folder's must be free (validation, conflict); events given the same place or the same new folder share it; each file is read once off the owner, bounded, its SHA-256 streamed, its header read and its interpretation read without developing, and must keep its signature while it is read and until it commits; a file whose bytes are a photograph's is linked to it, one whose name, length and fingerprint match a photograph whose original is not there relinks it (asset-source, its folder and history unchanged), a linked or relinked photograph in Removed is put back in the same change (asset-removal), a file another photograph names with other bytes fails with conflict, and any other becomes a photograph with its Original, capture row, source folder and moment in its event's folder; the job commits in batches, the first of one file, then up to 100 files or 5 s, never across an event, each one library change (the catalog-folder items of the folders it makes, parents first, then developed-asset, asset-source and pick items) announced as one event, clearing its picks; a file that fails is listed in failed and stays picked; picks on a removable volume are conflict (naming it in data) unless use_copies finds each a copy to verify or confirm_removable is set, and with use_copies a card's pick is developed from the first copy whose fingerprint matches (used), else from the card only with confirm_removable; an offline file fails with source-unavailable; nothing to develop is validation; job.cancel stops between files and keeps every batch committed; library.undo of a batch sends its photographs back, picks their files again and deletes the folders it made; a live retry answers the first job; a completed retry after restart reconstructs its stored terminal report, while an interrupted admission reports interruption and requires a fresh request ID; resource-limit when 4 library jobs already wait; the job records one event as it ends, however it ends, naming its job_id

Its generations run their GPU work in short slices so the interface keeps drawing. Each channel shifts by its own frozen stops on the scene scale Exposure uses, measured from Lightroom Classic, so white stays white and the cast lives in the midtones and shadows

Each channel shifts by its own frozen stops on the scene scale, measured from Lightroom Classic, adding to Temperature's

Its generations run their GPU work in short slices so the interface keeps drawing. mutation.notes: Every mutating method carries a mutation envelope. A method that changes an asset or a module's settings, which have a revision, carries revision: expected_revision must be that revision or the request is a conflict, and the method's revision_of says whose revision it is: asset, the asset its asset_id names, as asset.state answers it; draft, the asset its draft_id's draft is bound to; module-settings, the settings of the module its module_id names, as module.settings.read answers them. Every other mutating method carries request. request_id and actor are 1..128 characters. A retry with the same request_id and the same input returns the first answer, marked deduplicated: true, and emits no event; the same request_id with different input is a conflict. An asset change's request_id is unique per asset and is remembered durably with the change; Other request IDs are unique per method family, the method name without its last segment. Catalog mutations (library, picks, folders, collections, removal, versions, presets, batches, Locate, merges and artifact collection) retain input identity and outcomes durably, independently of asset deletion and owner cache eviction. Admitted asynchronous catalog jobs freeze their targets: live retries reuse the job, completed retries reconstruct its result, and work interrupted by restart reports interruption and requires a fresh request ID. Session-only and external-store mutations, including module settings, use the bounded owner cache with no restart or eviction guarantee; an expired settings retry conflicts on its revision.

paths.coordinates: A points parameter carries an ordered list of [x, y] positions in the content stage's normalized coordinates, in drawn order, where 1.0 is the stage's height on both axes, so a shape is the shape it looks like at any aspect ratio. Positions are not sorted and may repeat or reverse: a path is a path and not a function.
paths.notes: A posted path is snapped to a grid of stored_steps_per_unit steps per unit and decimated on that grid at a tolerance relative to the radius it is drawn with: decimation_tolerance_of_radius times the radius as stored on the same grid, and never less than decimation_tolerance_min. A stored position is therefore at most that tolerance plus grid_rounding from the position that was posted, and at one radius the same posted path always produces the same stored stroke. Decimation is idempotent: a desktop decimates at its radius before it posts, and a path posted undecimated arrives at the same stored bytes. A posted path holds at most posted_points_per_stroke positions, checked before decimation, and the stroke it decimates to at most points_per_stroke, checked after. A stroke is stored once under the hash of its contents and an entry's recipe references it by that hash, so a payload's strokes field holds addresses and never positions.

renderer.notes: session.state's renderer is {record, reason}, the same for every client of this owner. record gpu: the desktop's photo surface draws on its GPU, and reason is null; software is true when that GPU is the platform's software adapter (lavapipe on Linux, WARP on Windows), a rasterizer on the CPU, and is omitted otherwise. record reference: the CPU reference renderer draws the desktop's picture, slower, and reason says why: surface-pending before the desktop has drawn a photograph, which is when its photo surface checks its GPU stage; no-adapter when the GPU stage cannot run on this graphics device, when the host offers only a software adapter, which is not adopted and the desktop was not launched with --software-adapter, when the desktop's window draws on wgpu's OpenGL backend, on which the stage does not run, or when the desktop was launched with --no-gpu-render, which refuses it the same way; device-lost when the graphics device was lost, which nothing waits to recover. record reference with a null reason is an owner that draws nothing, such as luxforge-json, whose renderer is always the reference. The desktop reports it from its photo surface and the session reports it; no method sets it. A ready export's job.read result names the renderer that rendered its file in the same shape: record gpu with a null reason, or record reference with a null reason on an owner with no GPU, such as luxforge-json, and otherwise one of the reasons, one of export_reasons or the GPU plan's own code: requested when export.write asked for reference: true; surface-pending before the desktop has named the adapter its window draws with to its GPU tile worker, which it does once its photo surface has checked its GPU stage; no-adapter when the tile worker found no adapter or device it can render on; refused when the desktop was launched with --no-gpu-render; device-lost when the tile worker's device was lost, before or during the export, which then starts again on the reference; adapter-mismatch when the tile worker's adapter is not the one the window draws with; tiles-budget when the export's tiles would hold more than the tile worker's GPU budget; or the code of the GPU plan or stage that cannot draw the stack, such as no-program for a layer no GPU program replaces, or pipeline-failed.

session.notes: A method marked session_scoped: true acts only on the calling client's session, such as its draft, previewed entry, view, workspace or browse selection, which ends when the client's connection closes: call it on a connection that also sends what depends on it, never on a connection of its own.
